g.text: HC-SR04 - the exchange, the four conversions, and the image
STATUS: GREEN - 199 / 999 / 343 / 1375 mm, every one exact
SR_TRIG_LEN IS NOT SR_TRIG, and the two are different
the PIN BIT - which pad drives the trigger
the DELAY COUNT - how long it is held
the pin bit, released and read back
Both SR_TRIG and SR_TRIG_LEN exist in peasm's CONSTS, which is exactly why
naming the wrong one is easy and why a figure that printed
was wrong three ways at once: the +4
should be +5, the count is 601 not 600, and the constant has the wrong name.
The testbench pins 601 as an EQUALITY,
every datasheet window in print and still fails the act's own claim.
WHY THE ECHO IS CAPTURED AND NOT SAMPLED,
what makes this act safe at 4 m.
A receiver that samples the level and decides "there is
something there" has to poll, and a poll loop that is
long relative to the distance reading adds its own
uncertainty to every sample. A receiver that measures
the *width* does not care when it looked: the two
edges define the interval, and the interval is the
The same reason the counter is RESET at the rising edge
and READ at the falling edge rather than subtracted:
no 16-bit subtract, and this machine has no carry flag,
so a subtract is a four-case analysis on bit 7 and a
compare is the same analysis again. **One reset removes
independently, and for the same reason.
THE IDENTITY, and why it removes the multiply the plan
So the conversion is a multiply by
eleven of a ten-bit number, a multiply by eleven of a six-bit number, and one
A MULTIPLY BY ELEVEN IS FOUR DOUBLINGS AND TWO ADDS:
x -> 2x -> 4x -> 5x -> 10x -> 11x. No loop, no counter, no second
temporary - the multiplicand stays in Q throughout.
A DOUBLING IS THE CHEAPEST 16-BIT OPERATION THIS ISA HAS,
other 16-bit add it needs no both-zero guard. The carry out of lo+lo is bit 7 of
the ORIGINAL low byte, so one AND with 0x80 and one JNZ is the whole test; and
"the result is zero" means "nothing carried", because doubling zero cannot carry
and is the only way to reach zero. A general add of a variable IS different:
0 + 0 = 0 is not a carry, so the addends must be re-read.
the reason the conversion is mostly doublings.
the second term is 11 * 63 = 693. Recorded rather than assumed, because an
unnoticed overflow in the high byte is invisible from the outside - the answer
would still be a plausible millimetre figure.
THE FOUR MEASURED CONVERSIONS - and the one that ISOLATES the big term
"EXACT" MEANS TWO THINGS IN THIS ACT, AND RUN 3 IS THE
rounding error at all. A statement about the ALGORITHM, and the one the firmware's
2. THE ARITHMETIC IS EXACT AND THE ANSWER IS TRUNCATED.
199 is floor of it. So "PASS, an equality" is exact only AGAINST A TRUNCATING
EXPECTATION - and the testbench's "expected 199" IS that truncation, so the two
agree by construction rather than by luck.
8000 = 64 * 125 makes r = 0, so floor is the
identity and 1375 is the whole product. That is the one input where the word means
exact with nothing left over - and it is why four targets beat two.
A figure that said only "the conversion is exact" was making claim 1 and being read
as claim 2. Four runs is what makes that impossible to reproduce.
THE IMAGE - 387 words of 1024, and that is CORRECT
"387 words vs 1024 requested" READS AS A DEFECT AND IS NOT ONE.
the instruction memory is 1 024 words (IMEM_WORDS in the TB, pe_soc.v);
tools/fw/peasm.py pads the image to the requested width with 0xF000
is NOP, and says so in the generated file's own comment;
$readmemh into [0:1023] from a 387-word file leaves 637 words unwritten
reports it only in a WARNING, so the testbench now counts the file's own length
and asks $readmemh for exactly that many words, pre-filling with 16'hF000;
, so the fill is a no-op region behind a
The earlier symptom-only narration - an image that looked short - was a consequence
of the testbench asking $readmemh for more words than the file held. The length is
counted now, which is why the number is PRINTED rather than inferred from a warning.
WHY THESE FOUR TARGETS, and it is not "more is better".
5 816 us exercises the ten-bit path AND the high byte - an overflow here would be
invisible from the outside, because the answer would still be a plausible
8 000 us the r = 0 case: it ISOLATES 11*Q, it is the only width whose\n us x 11 overflows 16 bits, and it is the only one a\n high-byte mask slip can reach
THE MUTATION GAP IS NOW PARTLY CLOSED - two cases of 62, and the DIRECTION
An earlier revision of this figure said sr04 had NO mutation coverage. That was
true when written; it is corrected here rather than dropped. regress/
mutate_timing_tb.sh now carries 62 cases and TWO are sr04.
deletes the redundant LDI setting the trigger's ending level
- 600 clocks = 10.000 us SATISFIES the device's "> 10 us minimum", so a WINDOW check passes the mutant
drops ONE bit from the 0x3F mask on the high byte of us
1375 -> 1023 on 8 000 us ALONE, because bit 3 is set in 0x1F alone
Nothing yet perturbs the SMALL TERM,
floor(11r/64) - and the mutant that would do it, forcing the small term to zero, is
invisible in exactly the run one might expect. That is the blindness tabulated
below, and it is why "two cases" is a start rather than coverage.
